chapter: Taxi dance job and the Fiesta
title: Playing the Fiesta for Paul Bollier
summary: Williams recalls playing old quadrilles and cakewalk music for a Fiesta in the park, written out and rehearsed by a professor.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well you played for Paul Bollier recently, huh? I mean just a few years ago?
Yeah, when we had Fiesta. We had a Fiesta.
Well what did you play there? I miss that sometimes.
We played uh, focus. Quadrails. Mm-hmm.
Yeah, yeah. Just that kind of music, you know. They danced it, you know. Headed out in the park. You heard about it?
I heard about it, but I missed it. And uh, were you here then? I was here. Oh, you missed that man?
I don't know, I must've been sick or something.
You had some white people there.
Yeah, it was fun. Right in front of the auditorium. Mm-hmm.

On that old cakewalk and dancing with old people, you know. I didn't know the only one could do it, you see. I knew it. Mm-hmm. He got all that music. I don't know where he got it from. He said he remembered it, you see. And wrote it. Mm-hmm. And wrote it, you know. Mm-hmm. And now all our parts. Me, Pajou, Sonny Henry. Me, Pajou, Sonny Henry. And uh, Mario Pala. Yeah. Yeah. About six hours. Play.
What did the professor play? Piano? Piano. Professor Bobby? Yeah, piano.
He rehearsed on us about two weeks, you see.
After rehearsal the dances, you know what I'm saying. Did you play any of those dances when you were young, any of those dances? No.

They had cut that out, you see. It just had went out when I come in. We didn't play nothing but waltzes. And then all that was cut out. I never did see it. That was the first time I'd seen it. Mm-hmm. It's something like the square dance. Mm-hmm.
